name: Gauze-Requiem
geological_features: Geothermal hot springs at equatorial rift zones
specific_features: Thin ice fog perpetually veiling the surface like gauze
Bioluminescent ice algae creating faint green glow under the ice
description: Gauze-Requiem is a large ice world wrapped in a perpetual fog of ice crystals suspended in its thin atmosphere, creating a gauze-like veil that softens all visual detail and makes the surface appear to shimmer and shift. The fog never clears entirely, fed by sublimation from the vast continental ice sheets that cover ninety percent of the planet's surface. Beneath the fog, the ice sheets extend to depths of several kilometers, pressing down on bedrock that has not seen open sky in hundreds of millions of years. Only at the equatorial rift zones, where geothermal heat breaks through, does the ice thin enough to reveal the rock beneath.

The planet feels like a memorial. The fog muffles sound and sight, the ice preserves everything beneath it in frozen stillness, and the faint green glow of bioluminescent algae beneath the surface ice gives the landscape an underwater quality, as though the entire world has been submerged in some cold, quiet medium. The hot springs at the equatorial rifts are the only points of warmth, steaming pools of mineral-rich water that create oases of relative warmth in a frozen expanse that stretches to the horizons in every direction.

The bioluminescent ice algae represent the planet's most significant biological discovery. These organisms live within the ice itself, occupying thin liquid water films between ice crystals and photosynthesizing using the faint light that penetrates the upper ice layers. They grow in vast colonial sheets that produce enough bioluminescence to be visible from the surface as a diffuse green glow emanating from within the ice. The colonies are ancient—some are estimated to be millions of years old, growing imperceptibly slowly in their frozen medium.

The algae are endangered by the planet's gradual cooling trend, which is thickening the ice sheets and reducing the light available for photosynthesis. As the ice deepens, the algae colonies are being buried beyond the reach of any useful light, slowly starving in the frozen dark. The equatorial rift zones may serve as final refugia, but even these are narrowing as the ice advances. Gauze-Requiem is a world in the process of freezing its last life out of existence, a slow requiem played in dimming green light beneath kilometers of ice, witnessed only by the fog that drifts endlessly above.
